context: Horizon chart stack — data visualization showing 24-hour CPU usage across 8 servers with 3-band horizon folding encoding
first_impression: A deliberately designed monitoring chart with a coherent sequential blue palette and clean typographic hierarchy that reads as polished rather than default.
what_works: The Tol sequential blues palette (#9BD2E1 → #5AA5CC → #2166AC) is a purposeful, non-default choice that makes the three-band intensity encoding legible and harmonious. Typographic hierarchy is clear: bold 17px title, muted 12px subtitle, monospace 10px axis ticks — each layer quieter than the last.
what_doesnt: The alternating row backgrounds (white vs #f8f9fb) are so close in value they're nearly indistinguishable, providing no real visual separation — the thin separator lines do more work. The horizon band folding in the area function only maps band 0 correctly (clamped to step); darker bands stack on the same scale rather than truly folding, which means very high spikes don't render as multi-band overlaps the way a proper horizon chart should.
